1.title: Choosing Models, Deployments and Parameters
1.text: Welcome to Module three: Choosing Models, Deployments and Parameters. It covers the exam area Identify A I concepts and capabilities. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do three things. Identify an appropriate A I model, based on capabilities. Identify appropriate model deployment options and configuration parameters. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Identify A I concepts and capabilities (forty to forty-five percent). Exam format: a score of seven hundred on a scale of one to one thousand passes; check the exam page for the time. Validated against: the official A I nine oh one study guide, current skills measured.

1.title: The model catalog
1.text: The model catalog. Microsoft Foundry has a model catalog with more than ten thousand models from Microsoft, Open A I, Anthropic, Meta and others. The catalog has two categories. Foundry Models sold by Azure. Who hosts and sells it: Microsoft hosts and sells them under Microsoft Product Terms; billed through Azure. Why you pick it: Deep Azure integration, guaranteed support, enterprise service levels. Foundry Models from partners and community. Who hosts and sells it: Partners and the community; billed through the Azure Marketplace. Why you pick it: Specialized use cases and the newest ideas.

1.title: Choose a model by capability
1.text: Choose a model by capability. Pick the model whose capability matches the task, then weigh cost and speed. General chat, writing, summarizing, coding. Kind of model: Large language model (L L M). Notes: Most capable, most costly. Simple, high-volume, low-cost or fast tasks. Kind of model: Small language model (S L M). Notes: Cheaper and faster, less general. Hard multi-step problems: math, logic, planning. Kind of model: Reasoning model. Notes: Thinks before answering; slower; some settings are not supported. Understand images (and sometimes audio) in prompts. Kind of model: Multimodal model. Notes: Accepts more than text.

1.title: Choose a model by capability, continued
1.text: Choose a model by capability. Create images from a text description. Kind of model: Image-generation model. Notes: Output is an image. Turn text into vectors for semantic search. Kind of model: Embedding model. Notes: Output is numbers, not text. Speech to text or text to speech. Kind of model: Speech model or Azure Speech. Notes: Module five and ten. Exam tip: The exam asks "which kind of model" more than "which model name". Words to match: reasoning equals multi-step logic; multimodal equals images or audio in; embedding equals similarity search; image generation equals create pictures; S L M equals cheap and fast.

1.title: Deployment options
1.text: Deployment options. Before you use a model you deploy it. The deployment type decides where it runs, how you pay and how much traffic it can take. Standard (pay per token). Deployment types: Global Standard, Data Zone Standard, Standard. Meaning: You pay for the tokens you use. Global Standard can run in any Azure region and has the highest quota; Data Zone keeps processing in a data zone (U S, E U or A P A C); Standard stays within one Azure geography. Provisioned (reserved capacity). Deployment types: Global, Data Zone and Regional Provisioned. Meaning: You reserve capacity (throughput units) for steady, predictable, high volume.

1.title: Deployment options, continued
1.text: Deployment options. Batch (asynchronous). Deployment types: Global and Data Zone Batch. Meaning: Discounted processing of large jobs that can wait (up to about twenty-four hours; Global Batch is described with a fifty percent discount). Developer. Deployment types: Developer tier. Meaning: Evaluating fine-tuned models only: twenty-four-hour lifetime, no service level agreement. for current names, discounts and limits. Exam tip: "Start simple, pay per use" to Global Standard. "Predictable high volume, reserved capacity" to provisioned. "Large job, not urgent, cheaper" to batch. "Data must stay in the E U" to a Data Zone or regional type.

1.title: Configuration parameters
1.text: Configuration parameters. When you call a model you can set parameters that change how it answers. temperature. What it does: Controls randomness. The range is zero to two. Low (for example zero point two) gives focused, predictable answers; high (for example zero point seven or more) gives more varied, creative answers. Typical use: Low for facts and extraction; higher for ideas and stories. top p. What it does: Another way to control randomness: the model picks only from the most likely tokens that add up to this probability. It is similar to temperature. Typical use: Change temperature or top p, not both.

1.title: Configuration parameters, continued
1.text: Configuration parameters. max tokens ( max completion tokens for newer models). What it does: The maximum number of tokens the model may generate in the answer. Typical use: Cap cost and length; set it high enough for the expected answer or the reply is cut off (finish reason "length").

1.title: Configuration parameters, continued
1.text: Configuration parameters. Reasoning models use max completion tokens instead of max tokens, and do not support temperature, top p or the penalty parameters. The system message (module six) is not a number but also shapes the answer. Exam tip: "More creative" to raise temperature. "Same answer every time, factual" to lower temperature. "Reply stops in the middle" to raise max tokens. "Reasoning model" to no temperature setting.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. Fabrikam Outdoors needs a model that can describe photos that customers upload. Which kind of model fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: A multimodal model. A multimodal model accepts images (and sometimes audio) as part of the prompt.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A team needs a very fast, low-cost model for simple labeling at high volume. Which kind of model fits best? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: A small language model. Small language models are cheaper and faster and are enough for focused tasks.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. A product team wants product descriptions that vary and sound creative. Which setting change helps? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Raise the temperature. A higher temperature gives more varied and creative output.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. A company wants to keep its prompts and responses processed in the E U. Which deployment idea fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: A Data Zone deployment for the E U. Data Zone deployment types keep processing inside a data zone such as the E U.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. A reply from the model stops in the middle of a sentence and the finish reason is "length". What should be checked? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: The max tokens (max completion tokens) setting. The output hit the token limit, so the maximum must be raised.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. A team plans a large overnight job that is not urgent and wants a lower price. Which deployment category fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Batch. Batch processes large jobs asynchronously at a discount.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Which two categories does the Foundry model catalog have? Answer: Foundry Models sold by Azure, and Foundry Models from partners and community. Question two. Which deployment type is the usual starting point? Answer: Global Standard. Question three. What does a low temperature do? Answer: Gives more focused, predictable answers.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Which two settings should you not change together? Answer: Temperature and top p. Question five. What do reasoning models use instead of max tokens? Answer: max completion tokens. Question six. Which kind of model creates vectors for similarity search? Answer: An embedding model.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Catalog: ten thousand plus models; sold by Azure versus partners and community. Model kinds: L L M, S L M, reasoning, multimodal, image generation, embedding. Deployment: standard (pay per token, Global Standard first), provisioned (reserved), batch (discounted, asynchronous), developer (evaluation only). Data location: Global equals any region; Data Zone equals U S, E U or A P A C; Standard and Regional equals one geography. Parameters: temperature zero to two (low focused, high varied); top p similar. Reasoning models: max completion tokens; no temperature, top p. In the next module, we continue the course.
